analyst_view.overall: Early view: Almería are top on 29 points after a 1-0 win at Girona and are unbeaten at home (five wins, one draw) under Xavi García Pimienta, with Miguel de la Fuente the division's top scorer. Sporting are seventh but lost 2-1 at home to Valladolid, had a long injury list before that game and saw Juan Otero sent off. Marcos Luna's yellow-card ban should be served against Andorra on 14 November, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: Sporting's away games have averaged about 2.3 goals and they have won four of six on the road by staying compact, and Almería's last two matches finished 1-1 and 1-0. Almería at home are the likelier scorers, but a big total needs Sporting to open up.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. I lean slightly lower: García Pimienta's Almería build through the middle and took only two corners at Girona and three at Eibar, and Sporting's nine corners against Valladolid came with 62% of the ball, which they are unlikely to have at the leaders' ground.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. Sporting were booked heavily and had Otero sent off against Valladolid, but that was a high-risk home game; Almería picked up three yellows at Girona and two at Eibar. That leaves me close to the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Recent games support it: Girona-Almería had 26 shots, Eibar-Almería 30 and Sporting-Valladolid 35, so a total in the high 20s looks right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Almería had only three on target at Girona and one at Eibar, and many of the shots in these teams' games end up blocked, so I would expect fewer than ten on target.
